tools.name: list_tasks
tools.description: Use when the person wants paid data tasks from Kariaa (record clips, photos, voice, label text). The open DataHouse tasks: title, kind (video, photo, voice, text), the unpaid verification sample each wants and the rate paid work earns after verification. No key needed. Filter by file kind.

tools.name: get_task
tools.description: Use when the person picks a DataHouse task. One task in full: description, the task's own material (instructions: the sentences to read, texts to label, answers to rate), the unpaid verification sample with how-to steps and rules, allowed file kinds, the qualification questions (with ids, for apply_

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Use when you need to know who is signed in and what they still need. The account behind the key, whether the basics a task needs are in (legal name, phone, location, occupation), and today's usage.

tools.name: update_profile
tools.description: Use when the person gives the basics a task needs. Save the basics a task needs: legal first and last name, phone in E.164 (+1…), location as "City, Country", occupation (one to five titles, "student" is fine), language.

tools.name: apply_to_task
tools.description: Use when the person wants to join a DataHouse task. Join a DataHouse task for the person. `answers` maps each question id from get_task to the answer (a string, or a list for multiselect); every required question needs one. Optional preferred rate in their words ("$2 per clip"). One application per

tools.name: request_upload
tools.description: Use when you upload a sample file yourself. A one-time signed URL for ONE sample file of a task the person joined. PUT the raw bytes to upload_url with the returned headers, then call confirm_upload with the path. Kind must match the task; up to 100 MB; up to 10 files per task.

tools.name: confirm_upload
tools.description: Use right after the PUT from request_upload. After the PUT: register the object at `path` as a sample of the task. Returns how many samples are in and how many the task wants.

tools.name: remove_sample
tools.description: Use when the person wants to replace a staged sample. Take back one staged sample (a wrong or bad file) so another can be uploaded in its place. Only before submit_samples. file_id comes from confirm_upload, get_submission or my_submissions.

tools.name: get_upload_link
tools.description: Use when you cannot send file bytes yourself. A link to this task's upload page on kariaa.com, where the person signs in and picks their photos, voice notes or videos from their phone or computer. Use it whenever you cannot send the file bytes yourself (chat apps); give it to the person as is.

tools.name: add_text_sample
tools.description: Use when a DataHouse text task wants a written answer. For a text task: the person's written answer (20 to 20,000 characters), stored as a .txt sample.

tools.name: submit_samples
tools.description: Use when every sample is in and the person confirms. Send the staged samples of a task for review. Needs every sample the task asks for. Optional text_response for notes.

tools.name: my_submissions
tools.description: Use when the person asks how their DataHouse tasks stand. Every DataHouse task the person joined, newest first, with its stage (pending_review, sample_needed, in_review, approved, rejected).

tools.name: get_submission
tools.description: Use when the person asks about one DataHouse task. One task the person joined: stage, staged files, review outcome and the next step.

tools.name: my_earnings
tools.description: Use when the person asks about their Kariaa balance or payouts. The signed-in person's Kariaa balance, earnings, and payout requests. Platform earnings stay on those platforms.

tools.name: request_payout
tools.description: Use when the person asks to cash out their Kariaa balance. Payouts are bank transfers that the person requests on the Kariaa website; this tool returns the link and the steps. Never ask the person for bank details or tax IDs in chat.

tools.name: search_jobs
tools.description: Use when the person wants to find a job or paid work: live openings for a role, near a place or remote, newest relevant first, with links. kind "jobs" (default) searches job boards (LinkedIn, Indeed, Glassdoor, ZipRecruiter, national boards, remote-job sites); "paid_tasks" searches freelance project

tools.name: get_job
tools.description: Use when the person wants the details of one result from search_jobs: description, requirements, pay when stated, posted date and how to apply. Use it before applying, or to tailor a resume or cover letter to the posting.

tools.name: check_job_post
tools.description: Use when the person asks whether a job post, recruiter message or offer is legit or a scam. Returns warning signs (fees, upfront payments, personal email domains, link shorteners, pressure, requests for ID or bank details), each with the exact quoted line. Rule-based. Pass the text in English; trans

tools.name: estimate_pay
tools.description: Use when the person asks what a role pays, or whether an offer is fair, in a city or country. Returns what employers state, from recent postings that list pay: the typical range, how many postings it comes from, and examples with links. When there are too few, say so and research further yourself.

tools.name: save_job
tools.description: Use when the person wants to keep a job from search_jobs on their Kariaa list to come back to. Needs the person signed in.

tools.name: my_saved_jobs
tools.description: Use when the person asks for the jobs they saved: newest first, with whether each is still open. Needs the person signed in.

tools.name: list_platforms
tools.description: Use when the person asks where Kariaa finds paid work, or which freelance, bounty, competition or agent-task platforms they can use. Lists each platform with its category, whether the agent can apply there, and whether the person's account is linked.

tools.name: connect_platform
tools.description: Use when applying on a platform needs the person's own account there (get_job or apply_to_work said so). Returns the link where the person signs in to that platform or lets Kariaa set the account up. The person opens it; the agent never handles their password.

tools.name: apply_to_work
tools.description: Use when the person says yes to applying for a paid task, bounty, competition or freelance project from search_jobs (a job_id like "kaggle:titanic"). Applies as the person through their linked account. Ask them first and pass any note they want sent. For job openings with a UUID job_id, the person a

tools.name: add_work
tools.description: Use when the person has finished the work for a platform application (from apply_to_work) and wants it attached: the answer, write-up, code or links as text. Call submit_work after.

tools.name: submit_work
tools.description: Use when the person confirms the work on a platform application is complete and should be sent for review. Sends it as the person.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "connect_platform" references sensitive artifacts (password). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_upload_link, get_submission, check_job_post · Private data: list_tasks, get_task, request_upload, remove_sample, get_upload_link, get_submission, connect_platform · Public sink: request_upload, confirm_upload, get_upload_link, submit_samples, check_job_post, submit_work · Destructive: remove_sample.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_upload_link, get_submission, check_job_post · Private data: list_tasks, get_task, request_upload, remove_sample, get_upload_link, get_submission, connect_platform · Public sink: request_upload, confirm_upload, get_upload_link, submit_samples, check_job_post, submit_work · Destructive: remove_sample

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_upload_link" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Use when you cannot send file bytes yourself. A one-tap link to this task's upload page on kariaa.com, already signed in, where the person picks their photos, voice notes or videos from their phone or computer. Use it whenever you cannot send the file bytes yourself (chat apps). The link works once," → after: "Use when you cannot send file bytes yourself. A link to this task's upload page on kariaa.com, where the person signs in and picks their photos, voice notes or videos from their phone or computer. Use it whenever you cannot send the file bytes yourself (chat apps); give it to the person as is."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
